chunks: He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn reported to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim Majeelawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, from Nasr ibn Muzahim, from Amru ibn Sa'd, from Fudhail ibn Khudaij, from Kumail ibn Ziyad al-Nakha'i who said:

I was with the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), in the mosque of Kufa, and we had prayed the late evening prayer. He took my hand and we went out of the mosque. He walked until he reached the outskirts of Kufa, not speaking a word to me. When he reached the open desert, he sighed, then said:

O Kumail, indeed these hearts are containers, and the best of them are the most retentive. Remember from me what I say: People are of three kinds: a godly scholar, a student on the path of salvation, and riffraff — ignorant masses, followers of every croak, swaying with every wind. They never benefited from the light of knowledge, nor did they take refuge with a firm support.

O Kumail, knowledge is better than wealth: knowledge guards you while you guard wealth, and wealth is diminished by spending while knowledge grows with use. O Kumail, affinity for a scholar is the best way to worship God; it earns one obedience during one's life and beautiful reputation after one's death. O Kumail, the benefit of wealth disappears with its loss. O Kumail, the hoarders of wealth have died, while the scholars remain as long as time endures. Their bodies are gone, but their teachings are present in the hearts.

Alas! Alas! Indeed, here — and he pointed with his hand to his chest — there is abundant knowledge, if only I could find worthy carriers for it. But I have found a quick learner who is not trustworthy — he uses the instrument of religion for worldly gain, and seeks to dominate God's creation by God's proofs and to exploit His servants by His blessings, so that the weak-minded take him as a refuge instead of the guardian of truth. Or one obedient to wisdom but without insight into its depths, so doubt enters his heart at the first appearance of confusion. Behold! Neither this one nor that one is worthy.

So one is consumed by pleasures, easily led by the reins of desires, or one obsessed with accumulating and hoarding — not among the caretakers of religion. The closest resemblance to them is grazing cattle. Thus knowledge dies with the death of its carriers.

O God, indeed! The earth is never devoid of one standing with a proof — whether manifest and well-known, or hidden and unknown — lest God's proofs and clear signs become void. For indeed, those are the fewest in number but the greatest in importance. Through them God preserves His proofs, until they entrust them to their peers and plant them in the hearts of their likes. Knowledge has overwhelmed them with the realities of matters, so they experienced the spirit of certitude. They found easy what the affluent found difficult, and found comfort in what repelled the ignorant. They accompanied the world with bodies whose souls are attached to the highest station. Those are God's representatives on His earth and the callers to His religion.
Alas! Alas! How I long to see them! And I seek God's forgiveness for me and for you all. Then he withdrew his hand from mine and said: You may leave when you wish.

key_terms.عالم رباني: Godly/divine scholar - one whose knowledge is connected to God
key_terms.همج رعاع: Riffraff, ignorant masses who follow blindly

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say to Kumail about knowledge and the three types of people?
ai.summary: In this celebrated hadith, Imam Ali (AS) took his devoted companion Kumail ibn Ziyad outside Kufa and delivered a profound discourse on the three categories of people: the godly scholar, the student on the path of salvation, and the ignorant masses who follow every voice. He contrasted the superiority of knowledge over wealth, lamented the scarcity of worthy recipients for his vast knowledge, and affirmed that God never leaves the earth without a proof-bearer -- whether manifest or hidden -- through whom divine knowledge is preserved and transmitted to the hearts of the worthy.
